Assume full AC. Use the actual based earring $K\cup L\subset S^3$, its normal radius arc $\omega$, the compact exterior $X$ and a supplied $SO(3)$ bundle $P\to X$ with $w_2(P)=PD_{\mathbb F_2}[\omega]$ in the singular-data definition. Both boundary-torus restrictions of $P$ have nonzero $w_2$. The bundle admits a compatible extension to an order-two orbifold bundle over $(S^3,K\cup L)$ whose local isotropy is rotation by $\pi$, whose axis-orientation cover on each link component is nontrivial, and whose ordinary local singular residue is $\frac14\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)d\theta$ up to conjugation. It therefore supplies the compatible finite local data required by the order-two gauge-completion lemma.

For this completed data every connection has determinant-one stabilizer exactly $\{\pm1\}$. The bundle on the exterior also has an actual $U(2)$ lift with a chosen determinant line and determinant connection, as needed for cylinder holonomy functions. These statements concern the topology and analytic input data, not independence of the resulting choices or construction of Floer homology. The supplied-bundle existence clause of the original definition is retained; this result does not classify all singular extensions up to canonical isomorphism.

Assume full AC. Let a compact smooth pair $(M,S)$ without boundary of dimension three or four have $S$ of codimension two, and supply finite branched charts $(y,w)\mapsto(y,w^2)$ with group $\mathbb Z/2$ acting by $w\mapsto-w$, together with their compatible coordinate lifts. Supply a smooth orbifold metric and an $SO(3)$ bundle in these charts with nontrivial isotropy a rotation by $\pi$ about a line. Use its determinant-one gauge transformations: in each local quaternionic lift they obey $u(y,-w)=\rho u(y,w)\rho^{-1}$, where $\rho=\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$ and $\rho^2=-1$. These conjugation conditions are independent of the sign of the lift.

Finite-chart invariant Sobolev spaces $H^k$ are Hilbert spaces with smooth invariant density, compact $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ inclusion, and the usual dimension-three or dimension-four Sobolev product and embedding estimates. For $k\ge3$, the $H^{k+1}$ determinant-one gauge group is a Banach Lie group acting smoothly on the affine $H^k$ connection space. At an irreducible connection, Coulomb slices give a smooth unbased quotient and equation bundle; arbitrary connecting gauges between converging slice representatives have converging $H^{k+1}$ subsequences, up to their central ambiguity.

Every smooth first-order operator with scalar Clifford square, acting on these bundles and respecting the invariant local conditions, is Fredholm $H^k\to H^{k-1}$ on compact $M$. Its kernel and cokernel are smooth. A formally selfadjoint such operator $H$ has domain $H^1$ in $L^2$, compact resolvent and a complete real discrete spectrum of finite multiplicity. In particular this applies to the extended three-dimensional Hessian $H_B(\phi,b)=(d_B^*b,d_B\phi+*d_Bb)$, and in dimension four to $d_A^*\oplus\sqrt2d_A^+$.

On an infinite cylinder over the compact three-dimensional pair, suppose $H(t)$ has one fixed first-order principal part, shared by $H_\pm$, throughout the cylinder and differs from $H_\pm$ by smooth zero-order coefficients tending to zero with their first $k$ derivatives, while the selfadjoint limiting $H_\pm$ are invertible. The same assertion allows additional possibly nonlocal zero-order operators $R(t)$: every $\partial_t^aR(t)$ is bounded $H^j(Y)\to H^j(Y)$ for the needed integer orders, these bounds are uniform, and they converge on the ends in those operator norms; the two limiting full Hessians are selfadjoint and invertible on their $H^1$ domains. Then $\partial_t+H(t):H^k\to H^{k-1}$, including these additional terms, is Fredholm. The conclusion remains true on spaces weighted by $e^{\delta|t|}$ if $0\le\delta<\min\operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{spec}H_\pm)$. No index formula, nonlinear asymptotic convergence, transversality, trajectory compactification or Floer differential is asserted here.

Assume full AC. Supply a compact oriented three-dimensional order-two singular pair $(Y,K)$, compatible orbifold bundle data and determinant-one gauges as in the preceding completion lemma, and a fixed $U(2)$ lift on $Y\setminus K$ with fixed determinant connection. Suppose every connection in this singular configuration space has stabilizer $\{\pm1\}$. Use $H^k/H^{k+1}$, $k\ge3$.

There is a separable Banach space $\mathcal P$ of countable weighted sums of smooth cylinder functions supported away from $K$. For $\pi\in\mathcal P$ its function $f_\pi$ is bounded, smooth and gauge invariant, and its $L^2$ gradient $V_\pi$ is a smooth gauge-equivariant $H^k$ vector field. It is uniformly pointwise bounded by $C\|\pi\|_{\mathcal P}$, independently of the connection; its derivative is bounded on $L^2$ with the same type of uniform bound. Its spatial covariant derivatives have polynomial bounds in lower spatial covariant derivatives of curvature, with constants uniform on bounded perturbation sets.

The critical-point projection for $*F_B+V_\pi(B)=0$ is proper over compact subsets of $\mathcal P$ in the actual $H^k$ quotient. An open dense subset of $\mathcal P$ has only nondegenerate critical points; their set is finite. All critical connections are smooth in orbifold gauges. This result proves the critical set and not transversality, compactness or gluing for nonconstant trajectories. The existence of the stipulated global singular data and $U(2)$ lift is not asserted here.

Assume full AC. Fix the constructed earring data and a holonomy perturbation with finitely many nondegenerate critical points. There is a separable Banach space of further cylinder perturbations whose functions and all connection derivatives vanish at those critical points. Sufficiently small such perturbations retain exactly the same critical points and Hessians. A residual dense set of these perturbations makes every nonconstant finite-energy trajectory in every relative class regular, at every integer Fredholm index. The corresponding translation quotient is a smooth Hausdorff second-countable manifold of dimension $I-1$. In particular there are no nonconstant trajectories with $I\le0$.

Trajectories here are solutions in the actual unweighted cylindrical configuration spaces with critical asymptotics, and finite energy is the flow energy defined above. Establishing that arbitrary finite-flow-energy solutions have those asymptotics, and proving compactifications or gluing collars, remain separate claims. No orientability assertion is made here.

Assume full AC. Use the earring singular data, completed determinant-one gauge group $\mathcal G$, and fixed determinant lift constructed above. The restriction to the two core circles gives an exact sequence of component groups
$$0\longrightarrow\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\pi_0\mathcal G\longrightarrow(\mathbb Z/2)^2\longrightarrow0,$$
where the kernel generator is a degree-one gauge transformation supported in a ball disjoint from the singular link. For a loop in the unbased configuration quotient define $I$ as the index of its cylindrical ASD deformation operator with fixed invertible asymptotic Hessian, and define its topological energy period by twice the Chern–Simons drop, using inner product $-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbb C^2}$. Then
$$\mathcal E=\pi^2 I,\qquad I\in4\mathbb Z.$$
Both quantities vanish on the central stabilizer and descend to actual quotient loops.

Fix any perturbation in the nondegenerate critical class of the preceding critical-set lemma. For critical endpoints $\alpha,\beta$ and a relative path class $z$, let $I_z$ be the corresponding cylindrical index and $\mathcal E_z$ twice the drop of the perturbed functional. There is a constant $C$ depending on this fixed data, but not on $z,\alpha,\beta$, such that $|\mathcal E_z-\pi^2I_z|\le C$. For every finite upper index bound $D$, only finitely many endpoint pairs and relative classes of nonconstant gradient trajectories with $I_z\le D$ can occur, and their flow energies satisfy $0<\mathcal E_z\le\pi^2D+C$.

Here finite flow energy means $2\int_{\mathbb R}\|\partial_tB\|_2^2dt$ in temporal gauge, equivalently the perturbed topological energy. It does not mean the unrenormalized integral of curvature squared over the whole cylinder when its perturbed critical endpoints are nonflat. No trajectory compactness, regularity or gluing conclusion is part of this result.

Assume full AC. Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z/2$ act on $S^4=\mathbb R^4\cup\{\infty\}$ by rotation by $\pi$ in one normal two-plane, with fixed two-sphere. Supply a smooth equivariant $SO(3)$ bundle whose isotropy on that fixed sphere is a rotation by $\pi$. If $A$ is any nonflat equivariant anti-self-dual connection, its unbased invariant ASD complex has zero obstruction space and kernel dimension at least three. The corresponding flat reference bundle with constant fiber action has unbased index $-1$. Consequently the relative ASD index of this bubble against that flat reference is at least four.

At an ordinary point the analogous relative index loss is at least eight. These conclusions include every nonflat charge, not just BPST charge one.

More precisely, suppose two Fredholm ASD deformation operators on a compact four-orbifold, or on a cylinder with identical invertible limiting Hessians, have bundles identified away from one standard ball or one such order-two quotient ball. Form the comparison bundle $Q$ on $S^4$ (respectively $S^4/\Gamma$) by gluing their local ball bundles with that boundary identification, and let $Q_0$ be the constant reference. Then their index difference is exactly $\operatorname{ind}D_Q-\operatorname{ind}D_{Q_0}$. Thus when $Q$ is an actual nonflat ASD bubble the preceding lower bounds apply. The result does not assume that every degeneration has such a comparison until point-removal and topological identification have been proved for that degeneration.

Assume full AC. Use the fixed earring orbifold data, metric and an allowed holonomy perturbation in a bounded set of the constructed perturbation space. On every compact subcylinder, a sequence of smooth perturbed ASD trajectories with a common upper bound on flow energy has, after gauges and a subsequence, a limit away from finitely many points. On that punctured subcylinder the convergence is strong $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for every finite $p$ in local gauges. The limiting connection extends across those points as a smooth perturbed ASD connection on an actual smooth orbifold bundle. The lost energy at each point is a positive multiple of $8\pi^2$ at an ordinary point and a positive multiple of $4\pi^2$ on the singular surface, in the fundamental trace convention.

All concentrated bundles are accounted for by finitely many nonflat ordinary or order-two invariant ASD sphere bubbles with flat matching collars and no additional clutching contribution on the intervening necks. Thus the cylindrical index difference is the sum of their actual relative indices, at least eight per ordinary bubble and at least four per invariant bubble. In particular every concentration point has index loss at least four. If there are no concentration points, convergence on smaller closed subcylinders is smooth in orbifold gauges. The statement is local in the cylinder direction and does not assert convergence at its infinite ends or any nonlinear gluing collar.

Assume full AC. For the constructed earring data choose one of the all-index regular holonomy perturbations with its finite nondegenerate critical set. Every smooth trajectory of finite flow energy has a single critical orbit at each infinite end and, in actual determinant-one orbifold gauges, converges to representatives exponentially in every Sobolev order. For every fixed integer index bound there are only finitely many possible endpoint pairs and relative classes of nonconstant trajectories.

Sequences of trajectories of index one or two have, modulo translations, subsequences converging to finite broken trajectories without bubbles. The total index is the sum of the positive indices of the nonconstant levels. Thus the index-one translation quotient is a compact finite set; an index-two sequence has either a smooth unbroken limit or precisely two index-one levels. This statement identifies sequential limits and does not yet assert gluing collars or orientations.

Assume full AC and the actual all-index regular earring perturbation. Every ordered broken pair of index-one trajectories has a gluing collar of index-two unparametrized trajectories. Each sufficiently broken index-two trajectory belongs to precisely the collar of its broken limit. The glued relative class is the actual concatenation class. Together with the unbroken moduli, these collars make the index-two compactification a compact one-dimensional manifold with boundary the ordered broken pairs. The smooth structure is its ordinary smooth structure in the interior and the collar smooth structure at its boundary. No assertion of analyticity in an arbitrarily preassigned exponential neck coordinate is made.

Assume full AC and the constructed earring data. The real determinant line of the cylindrical ASD operator is orientable on every fixed-endpoint trajectory configuration component. One can choose rank-one integral orientation modules for the critical points and compatible determinant identifications for every relative trajectory class. They are compatible with concatenation, gauge equivalence and the nonlinear broken-trajectory collars. With the translation orientation removed, the signed boundary of an index-two compactification is the signed sum of its ordered index-one broken pairs. Consequently the integral signed differential defined by those pairs has square zero. Choices of bases in the critical orientation modules change the resulting complex by the corresponding diagonal signs.

Assume full AC. Integral earring instanton complexes formed from any two regular orbifold metrics and allowed regular holonomy perturbations of the fixed based earring data are related by continuation chain maps. A map depends only on its endpoints up to chain homotopy and the declared determinant-orientation sign choices. Continuation maps compose up to chain homotopy, and the maps in reverse directions are inverse chain homotopy equivalences. Transport under an isotopy of the based knot and its earring data gives the corresponding homology isomorphism. This statement concerns the singular instanton complex; it makes no assertion about sutured-closure independence, a knot-detection theorem or an instanton surgery formula.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: By [F1] the prescribed singular data are realized by actual finite-group charts and determinant-one gauges, with no reducible stabilizers. By [F2] the critical points of the perturbed Chern–Simons functional form a finite nondegenerate set, and its genuine singular trajectory equation has the stated Fredholm Sobolev realization. All smooth finite-flow-energy trajectories have the critical asymptotics in those spaces by [F3]. Thus the zero sets used to define the complex are actual smooth finite-dimensional regular moduli, rather than only formal expected-dimensional spaces.

Let $o_\alpha$ be the rank-one integral orientation module of a critical point from [F4] and set $C=\bigoplus_\alpha o_\alpha$. This is finite free. For each ordered critical pair, sum the signed module maps over every relative class of index one. There are only finitely many such classes and finitely many trajectories in each translation quotient by [F3]. Hence this is a well-defined integral homomorphism $d:C\to C$. The index periods are divisible by four, so the relative grading modulo four from [F3] gives this differential degree one in the cochain convention; no unsupported absolute integer grading is claimed. Choosing bases of the modules identifies this complex with the displayed generator convention of the Definition.

For any two endpoint critical points, take all index-two relative classes. Their finite union of compactified translation quotients is a compact oriented one-manifold by [F3]–[F4]. Its boundary consists exactly of all ordered index-one broken pairs, without bubbles, missing collar sheets or constant nonregular limiting levels. The actual signed boundary comparison in [F4] identifies its algebraic boundary sum with one fixed convention sign times the corresponding coefficient of $d^2$. That boundary sum is zero. This holds for every endpoint pair, so $d^2=0$ over $\mathbb Z$, not only modulo two. No surgery or sutured excision theorem is used in this argument.

The continuation theorem [F4] constructs finite signed counts for the actual nonautonomous equation, its chain maps and inverse chain homotopies between any two regular metrics and allowed perturbations. Its finite-parameter energy estimate and low-dimensional compactness supply the composition and homotopy relations, including the constant-continuation identity. Therefore the homology of this finite free cochain complex is independent of those choices with the stipulated determinant-orientation sign convention.

An isotopy of the based knot and its earring data transports the actual branch charts, exterior bundle, holonomy perturbations and gauge-fixed operators. The pullback chain identification and the continuation equivalence of [F4] give the asserted isotopy isomorphism. The sign choices agree with the orientation-module convention in step 2.1. This proves precisely the analytic construction and invariance in the original Statement. Sutured-closure independence, the KHI rank detector, resolution-cube maps, instanton L-space surgery and a distinguished canonical class remain their own separate obligations; none has been inferred from this complex construction.

Assume full AC. For any smooth based link $L\subset S^3$ with a chosen nonzero normal vector at its marked point, add the small meridional earring on that marked component and its joining arc. With the corresponding determinant-one singular bundle data, finite nondegenerate critical points and all-index regular holonomy perturbations give a finite free integral cochain complex. Its differential counts all index-one classes and has square zero; its homology, denoted $I^\natural(L;\mathbb Z)$, is independent of regular metric and perturbation and invariant under isotopy of the based link data, with the same orientation sign convention as for knots. For a knot it agrees with the singular knot complex already constructed.

For the standard $n$-component unlink with a marked component, $n\ge1$, this group is free of rank $2^{n-1}$. It has a chosen representative complex with zero differential and sphere-pole generators, in the even relative degrees of the unlink model. This theorem does not supply a canonical tensor-product identification under arbitrary cobordisms, saddle maps, an exact triangle or a KHI identification.

Assume full AC. In $[0,m]\times S^3$ take a finite composite of the specified local skein saddles and standard disk births or deaths, with every surface component meeting a temporal boundary and every local ball disjoint from the fixed basepoint earring and its radius arc. Include the vertical earring annulus in the surface $\Sigma$, and put $\Omega=[0,m]\times\omega$. There are actual marked order-two orbifold $SO(3)$ data on this four-dimensional pair, product in the temporal end collars, with surface isotropy rotation by $\pi$ and ordinary residue $\frac14\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)d\theta$. Their sheet cover on $\Sigma$ is dual modulo two to $\partial\Omega\cap\Sigma$. The exterior bundle has $w_2=PD_{\mathbb F_2}[\Omega]$ and an actual $U(2)$ lift with determinant class $PD_{\mathbb Z}[\Omega]$. Every determinant-one connection has central stabilizer only. The endpoint restrictions are admissible based-link earring data, with nontrivial axis cover on the two marked components and trivial axis covers on the other oriented end components.

The assertion is existence of compatible backgrounds for these actual surfaces. It asserts no four-dimensional count, cobordism-map invariance or sutured nonvanishing theorem. Whole end collars may be fixed for a chosen background. Cut pieces of that background retain their actual restriction identifications.

Assume full AC. Fix a marked earring cobordism made from the specified saddles and standard disk births or deaths, initially with every surface component meeting a temporal boundary, or any finite composite of such cobordisms with its actual glued background. Fix the actual orbifold and exterior determinant background, fixed regular nondegenerate critical data on its based-link ends, and a compact finite-dimensional parameter manifold with corners $P$. Boundary faces may prescribe broken metrics only along admissible based-link cuts carrying the same product data. Assume the prescribed face data already have regular counts and collars and agree on their corners. Then one can choose gauge-covariant bulk holonomy perturbations, product with the fixed gradient perturbations on the ends and relative to those face data, so all finite-energy fixed-endpoint cobordism moduli spaces are regular, for every marked relative class. In total expected dimensions zero and one, their unions over ALL relative classes are finite oriented sets and compact oriented one-manifolds with the expected broken ends and metric-face ends. Every such end has an exhaustive nonlinear collar and the determinant boundary sign is the ordered composition sign. Thus these counts give integral chain maps and relative chain homotopies; compositions are represented by the admissible stretching families with their actual orientation identifications.

No cut with a reducible critical point is included in this theorem. It does not prove the reducible unknot-cut vanishing, the triple-saddle degree-one cap count, or the identification of saddle maps with the Khovanov Frobenius operations.

Assume full AC. Let three based smooth links in the oriented three-sphere agree outside a ball disjoint from the earring and its marking arc, and differ there by the three cyclic skein tangles. Give their based-link instanton complexes compatible admissible marked backgrounds. The oriented saddle cobordism counts define an integral exact triangle on their instanton homology. With the actual relative grading shifts, the triangle is represented by a quasi-isomorphism of a mapping cone with the third instanton complex. These maps, null homotopies and mapping-cone comparisons can be chosen relative to any finite collection of already compatible disjoint saddle and continuation families.

Assume full AC and the actual based-link earring count, composition and integral skein operations of the named suppliers. Fix ONE finite planar resolution diagram, its marked base component and its finite collection of planar saddle cobordisms. Use the actual compatible backgrounds and determinant orientations relative to their common marked collars. Then the free integral unlink groups and these ACTUAL saddle maps admit simultaneous identifications with the reduced Frobenius module of
$$A=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^2),\qquad 1=v_+,\quad x=v_-,\quad |v_+|=0,\quad |v_-|=2\pmod4.$$
An unlink with one marked component and m other ordered components has group A tensor ... tensor A, with m factors; the marked factor is the quotient A/(x)=Z. A disk birth inserts v_+, and a disk death has epsilon(v_+)=0, epsilon(v_-)=1. On two unmarked components the merge and split are
$$\mu(1\otimes1)=1,\quad\mu(1\otimes x)=\mu(x\otimes1)=x,\quad\mu(x\otimes x)=0,$$
$$\Delta(1)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x,\qquad\Delta(x)=x\otimes x.$$
A merge with the marked component is the quotient action 1 tensor 1 to 1, 1 tensor x to zero; a split of the marked component sends 1 to 1 tensor x. The bases are primitive integral bases, not rational bases recovered after a rank computation. Reordering the unmarked components permutes their even factors.

These identifications are compatible with the actual finite planar vertex and saddle identifications used for that diagram, including the common marked collar. They do not assert a split-link excision theorem, invariance under arbitrary unlink concordances or arbitrary unlink-motion loops, or a new analytic construction beyond the named actual count suppliers. The cube's ordered orientation-line edge signs are retained; they are not replaced by independently chosen signs for each occurrence of a saddle.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

Let $(D,p)$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a knot with a basepoint $p$ away from the crossings, and let $C(D)$ be its normalized integral Khovanov cochain complex. At each resolution state, let $X_p$ act by multiplication by $X$ on the tensor factor for the circle containing $p$, and by the identity on every other circle factor. The basepoint action is the direct sum of these statewise maps. Define the reduced cochain complex by
$$\widetilde C(D,p):=C(D)/\operatorname{im}(X_p),$$
with the same cohomological grading and with reduced quantum degree $\widetilde j=j-1$ for the class represented by a state whose basepoint circle is labelled $1$. Its cohomology is the reduced integral Khovanov cohomology $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p)$. The unknot is normalized so that its reduced group lies in bidegree $(0,0)$.

Equivalently, cut the based knot at $p$ to a one-interval tangle. Put $M=\mathbb Z$ in quantum degree $0$ with $X\cdot1=0$. A resolution with $k$ closed circles and the distinguished interval is assigned $\mathcal A^{\otimes k}\otimes M$. An edge that merges a circle into the interval uses $m_M(1\otimes1)=1$ and $m_M(X\otimes1)=0$; an edge that splits the interval uses $\Delta_M(1)=X\otimes1$, where the circle factor is written first and the interval factor second. Edges not meeting the interval use $m$ or $\Delta$. This based tangle cube is the quotient complex above, with the stated quantum shift.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram, order its crossings as $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and form the direct sum of state modules $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$ over all functions $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$. Here $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, each crossing is changed from its A-smoothing at $0$ to its B-smoothing at $1$, and the edge map is the multiplication $m$ for a merge or comultiplication $\Delta$ for a split, multiplied by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ on the edge at $c_j$. Then the sum $d$ of all edge maps satisfies $d^2=0$.

If the filtration on every $C_n$ is finite, the spectral sequence of the filtered chain complex stabilizes pointwise and naturally abuts to $H_n(C)$ with its image filtration. This homology filtration is finite, exhaustive and separated. No uniform filtration bound in n is required.

derivations.claim: **The multi-saddle parameter spaces and their entire boundary.** Use the resolution labels of the reflected diagram, with an edge increasing one coordinate. Write $C_v$ for the actual based-link complex of that planar resolution. For $v<w$, let $S$ be its set of changed crossings, $k=|S|$. Put one standard saddle at time $\tau_j$ in each of its disjoint crossing balls; collisions of times are allowed, since the spatial balls are disjoint. Divide simultaneous translation out of $\mathbb R^S$, giving a parameter space of dimension $k-1$. Its broken compactification is constructed as follows. A boundary chart is indexed by an ordered partition $S=B_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup B_l$: retain the centered finite times within each block, and give successive block centers gaps $T_r$, with boundary coordinate $q_r=e^{-T_r}\ge0$. On chart overlaps centering changes a gap by a smooth bounded function of the retained block times, so $q_r$ changes by a smooth positive factor; two successive subdivisions give the same ordered gaps. These are manifold-with-corners charts. They cover a compact space: in any sequence normalize one time, pass to a fixed order of the finitely many labels, and select successive gaps which are bounded or diverge to positive infinity. The bounded clusters give finite centered limits after subdivision into their own bounded/divergent clusters, and there are at most $k$ labels. This proves sequential compactness in these finite partition charts; their countable coordinate basis and Hausdorff gap coordinates give compactness. Its facets are exactly the two nonempty ordered blocks. Such a facet is the product of the two smaller saddle parameter spaces, with the intermediate resolution as its cut; higher corners are their ordered iterates. Actual metrics are the fixed saddle metrics translated to these times, with product critical collars between separated blocks. Use their existing product metrics on every boundary chart and extend over the remaining compact interior by a finite partition in the convex cone of positive metrics. Here the background compatibility can be made literal. Put the planar resolution curves and the saddle surfaces in projection-plane times time; a local saddle has graph $t=x^2-y^2$ and normal coordinate $z=0$. The constant viewing-normal vector $\partial_z$ is a nonzero normal section on every such panel and every unchanged planar strand strip. Fix the product normal model on the separate earring annulus. Thus the normal splitting in [F2] uses the SAME section on every cube face, rather than separately chosen graph-spine sections. The sheet cover is cut along the SAME vertical marking arcs, outside all crossing balls. Construct the exterior determinant line by the degree-one angular Thom clutch around the fixed marking rectangle; it is the fixed product line outside the crossing balls and the fixed trivial line inside each ball, since the rectangle misses them. On the normal tube use the explicit common sheet gluing $\rho(v)w=v\bar w$ of [F2], with these normal coordinates. Restriction at an intermediate resolution, and commuting two disjoint saddles, now preserve these very transition functions and their determinant trivializations. Hence all backgrounds and all corner identifications agree as actual gluing data. Relative perturbations from [F2], by induction on $k$, therefore agree on all corners.

**The total differential and the exact edge signs.** Orient $\mathbb R^S/\mathbb R$ by the ordered crossing coordinates together with the positive simultaneous-translation direction. Retain the parameter orientation line instead of making separate arbitrary signs on its faces. At vertex $v$ tensor $C_v$ with the top exterior line $E_v=\bigwedge^{|v|}\mathbb Z^{\{j:v_j=1\}}$, of parity $|v|$. For an edge increasing $j$, identify the line map with insertion of $e_j$ and reorder into increasing crossing order. Its sign is exactly $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v_i}$. For a larger $S$, use the analogous ordered exterior insertion and the parameter orientation line to define the signed zero-dimensional count $D_{wv}$. Include the vertex differential as $D_{vv}$. The relative grading shift makes each total map odd: its unshifted parity is $1-k$, from its $k-1$ parameters and the even local saddle degree, whereas exterior insertion changes parity by $k$. A one-dimensional parameter moduli space has only end-trajectory breaks and the two-block facets of step 1.1; it has no unlisted bubbles or extra class ends by [F2]. Ordered determinant excision identifies each boundary count with its corresponding composition $D_{wu}D_{uv}$. Its sign is precisely the exterior shuffle sign: move the ordered first block past the second in the exact sequence of their time-coordinate spaces, separating the positive gap and translation factors. For one element in each block this is the anticommutation $e_ie_j=-e_je_i$; for general blocks it is its repeated shuffle. Thus the algebraic boundary-zero identity is the coefficient of $D^2$ at every vertex pair. The finite direct sum $T=\bigoplus_v C_v\otimes E_v$ with $D=\sum_{v\le w}D_{wv}$ is an integral complex. Checkerboard boundary orientations of the planar regions orient all the surfaces consistently; their product determinant orientations are those of [F4]. If the skein labels are initially decreasing, reversing all labels contributes the fixed edge factor $(-1)^{j-1}$, removed by the vertex sign $(-1)^{\sum_j(j-1)v_j}$. The displayed increasing edge sign is therefore literal in [F5]'s convention.

**Why this total complex is the original instanton complex.** Leave one crossing unresolved and keep the other resolution parameters. The total complex obtained by resolving that crossing decomposes into its two face totals and their off-diagonal saddle-family map; by step 2.1 this is its actual mapping cone, with the indicated shifts. Use [F3]'s cone comparison on that crossing relative to every already fixed disjoint saddle family. Its components with other crossings changed are the counts over the same disjoint time families, with the local two-saddle homotopy and three-saddle pentagon inserted. Their boundary strata are exactly those already specified in [F3] and step 1.1. The relative perturbations agree on their common faces, and their boundary formulas are exactly the assertion that these components give a filtered chain map from the partially unresolved total to this cone. Filter both by the other crossings. On its associated graded this map is the vertexwise cone quasi-isomorphism of [F3]. A finite filtered comparison with quasi-isomorphic associated graded is itself a quasi-isomorphism: induct on the filtration length, use the short exact sequence of a final filtration piece and its quotient, and chase the long exact sequences in cohomology. No convergence of an infinite filtration is used. Resolve the crossings one at a time. This gives a composite quasi-isomorphism between $T$ and the original complex $C(K)$, including the zero-crossing case, which is the identity. Hence $H(T,D)\cong I^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$. This is an actual filtered-cone construction, not an inference that matching vertex ranks determines the abutment.

**The first two pages.** Filter $T$ by $F^pT=\bigoplus_{|v|\ge p}C_v\otimes E_v$. Every count increases the number of resolved coordinates, so this is a bounded filtration by subcomplexes. The local tetrahedral smoothing chart interchanges its two planar pairings when the over- and under-strands are reflected; these are precisely the A- and B-resolutions of the reflected diagram in [F5]. derivations.claim: In the chosen closure, the standard marked circle meets $\bar R$ once, so $c_1(w)$ evaluates oddly on $\bar R$. The ordinary admissible theory in [F3] therefore applies. This proves well-definedness of the rational group used here, without choosing a canonical basis or confusing it with the doubled full ordinary group.

For a nontrivial smooth classical knot, the published genus/rank consequence in [F5] gives $\dim_{\mathbb Q}KHI(K;\mathbb Q)>1$. This is the established nonvanishing/decomposition input, explicitly imported rather than deduced from the already resolved singular complex or integral cube.

citations.quote: If a regular link diagram on $S^2$ is connected and alternating, then the represented link is nonsplit.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every connected reduced alternating diagram $D$ of an oriented link $L$ realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link: $c(D)=c(L)$.

A **2-tangle diagram** is a regular diagram in a disk of two properly embedded tangle arcs and possibly finitely many closed tangle components, with four specified endpoints on the disk boundary; the arcs and circles are disjoint in the represented 3-ball, while their projections may have crossings. A **flyping circle** is a simple closed curve in the projection sphere whose intersection with the diagram consists of exactly three points, exactly one of which is a crossing; the circle is transverse to both branches at that crossing and to the diagram at the other two points. A small annular neighborhood of this circle has two complementary tangle disks. A **flype** fixes the tangle in one disk, interchanges which pair of strands crosses in the annular neighborhood, and turns over the tangle in the other disk: its projected tangle is reflected and all its over-under crossing data are reversed. This turnover is a half-turn in three-dimensional space about an axis in the projection sphere. Component orientations are transported by this motion, and the exterior diagram is fixed. The move with the opposite choice of fixed disk is also allowed; a disk containing no crossings is allowed. A flype whose fixed tangle has no crossings is called an **entire flype**. Diagrams are drawn on the oriented projection sphere; a **sphere planar isotopy** is an orientation-preserving smooth isotopy of that sphere carrying the decorated diagram. A plane diagram is obtained by choosing a point of the sphere outside the projection and deleting it. At each crossing of a link diagram, a **crossing ball** is a small 3-ball in which the overpass lies on the upper hemisphere and the underpass lies on the lower hemisphere, with the rest of the link outside that ball. Replacing all crossing disks by upper hemispheres or by lower hemispheres gives the shifted projection spheres $S_+$ and $S_-$. A **saddle disk** in a crossing ball is a properly embedded disk whose boundary meets each of the two hemispheres in two arcs and whose interior passes across the equatorial crossing disk. For a closed embedded surface transverse to the link and to $S_+$ and $S_-$, each component $C$ of its intersection with either shifted sphere has a **bubble word**: read once around $C$, recording $P$ each time it crosses the link and $S$ each time it passes through a crossing ball along a saddle disk. The surface is in **bubble standard position** if every such word is nonempty and no word records the same crossing ball more than once. A **Conway sphere** is an embedded sphere meeting the link transversely in four points; it is in crossing-ball standard position when its intersection with the crossing balls consists of saddle disks and its shifted-sphere intersection curves satisfy the bubble-standard conditions.

The turnover convention is the one in Kindred's Definition 2.9 and Figure 1. In particular, an entire flype permits viewing the whole diagram from the opposite side of the sphere, as in his Definition 2.11. Closed components inside a tangle disk are carried along with its arcs.

Retain the actual cap-ball parameters and boundary collars, the global oriented component names, and any distinguished root point away from the sphere boundaries.

There is a comparison of the two systems by finitely many sphere surgeries, suppression of trivial capped connectors, and passage to a common refinement. Every other cap of a suppressed trivial connector is retained in its actual order, including at a connector of valence greater than two. It is **alternating** when successive crossing visits along each component switch between overpasses and underpasses. It is **reduced** when no complementary region of the projection sphere has a crossing more than once on its boundary. A connected alternating diagram that is reduced is a **reduced alternating link diagram**.

derivations.claim: Identify the two represented oriented links with one smooth link $L$ by the given isotopy. It is nonsplit by [F1]. Full AC supplies the choice hypotheses of [F2] and [F5]. The identification retains the actual oriented component correspondence to be used in all capped factors.

If $L$ is the unknot, [F2] forces both diagrams to have zero crossings. A connected crossing-free diagram is one embedded oriented circle on the projection sphere, and the two such circles are carried to one another by a sphere planar isotopy with their orientations transported. This proves the conclusion in this case. Henceforth $L$ is nontrivial and both diagrams have positive crossing count.

In either diagram cut along a simple circle meeting the diagram transversely in two ordinary points whenever both sides contain crossings. Cap each cut arc by a crossing-free arc in its cap disk, carrying the endpoint pairing and orientation. Both capped shadows are connected: an additional shadow component on either side would already have been a separate component of the original shadow. Their crossing sets partition that of the piece being cut. The capped diagrams are alternating: the proper strand in a two-ended disk has an even number of crossing encounters, since the total number is twice the number of crossings and each closed component contributes an even number; thus its first and last encounters have opposite status. Closing its ends introduces no new encounter.

The capped diagrams are reduced. Indeed, a nugatory separator through an old crossing in a capped diagram can be moved off the crossing-free cap disk: each part in that disk lies in one of the two complementary disks of its cap arc and can be pushed to the boundary collar. It would then give a nugatory separator through the same crossing in the original piece, contrary to reducedness. The cut and caps have smooth product collars. In the represented link they are the usual twice-punctured decomposition sphere and its standard trivial-arc cap balls.

Repeat these cuts in the capped pieces, retaining their cap-ball parameters and attachment collars. A later cut is moved off the interiors of earlier cap balls using their crossing-free trivial-arc product collars; equivalently shorten each artificial cap into its boundary collar before choosing the next cut. Lifting the resulting finite diagrammatic connected-sum decomposition gives pairwise disjoint decomposition spheres in the original link. Termination is finite: if a piece with $a+b$ crossings is replaced by two pieces with $a,b>0$ crossings, the sum of squared crossing counts falls by $2ab$. The final positive-crossing capped diagrams are therefore connected, reduced, alternating and have no two-point splitting circle with crossings on both sides. Crossing-free trivial connectors are suppressed while retaining all other attachment collars.

Every positive-crossing terminal factor is nontrivial by [F2]; otherwise its reduced alternating crossing count would be zero. It is nonsplit by [F1] and prime by [F4]. Thus the two finite systems just constructed, with their actual cap parameters, factor diagrams and oriented component labels, satisfy exactly the decomposition hypotheses of [F5].

Apply the comparison part of [F5] to those two systems in $L$. It provides the corresponding capped prime factors and actual oriented factor isotopies needed by its lift, including all refinements and suppressed trivial connectors. The correspondence transports the fixed global component names and attachment data from step 1.1.

For each corresponding pair of prime factor diagrams needed in that comparison, apply the imported theorem [F3] to the orientation-preserving pair map induced by its actual capped-factor isotopy. This supplies a finite sequence of the prescribed flypes and sphere planar isotopies whose transported oriented component bijection is precisely the one specified by the comparison. These are supplied maps, not arbitrary unlabelled symmetries of the prime factors.

The lift in [F5] now applies with its exact marked prime input supplied by step 3.2. It realizes the attachment transfers and prime sequences by finitely many allowed flypes and sphere planar isotopies, giving $D_0$ to $D_1$ with the fixed oriented component correspondence. Together with the crossing-free case, this proves the stated theorem for connected reduced alternating diagrams, including composite links.
